text: Hey. This thing is making weird noises. Is that fire? Uh-oh. It's about to explode. What should you do? According to the 2011 American Housing Survey, 97% of households in the U.S. have a microwave oven. So it's not surprising that microwave-related injuries are common. Some people estimate that more than 20 Americans are treated in hospital emergency departments every day due to microwave oven injuries. And even when these ovens observe the Food and Drug Administration's safety measures, malfunctions can make these little radiation boxes fatal. These ovens produce microwaves, a form of non-ionizing radiation that cannot change bodies' genetic composition, like ionizing radiation can. But microwaves speed up molecules in substances, and they can be dangerous to your body. "I started a fire".

video_title: How to Survive a Malfunctioning Microwave
text: A dangerous reaction happens inside the oven, and the only thing keeping your flesh away from radiation is that little door. And it is essential that the oven works correctly. Your eyes and testicles are particularly vulnerable to microwaves because they have relatively low blood flow, so they cannot cool down quickly enough to avoid damage. A gap or crack in the door can leak enough microwaves to cause cataracts and severe skin burns. So, if you see any cracks on the door or you suspect that the door is not closing properly, do not turn on the microwave oven. And send it to be serviced.

video_title: How to Survive a Malfunctioning Microwave
text: We all know the first commandment of using a microwave oven. "Who is on the Lord's side?" Never put metal inside. But guess what. The microwaves in the oven are produced by a strong metal box known as a magnetron. But if you add some other metal, especially thin metal pieces, the microwave radiation will move the electrons in the metal back and forth, producing heat inside the metal, which will cause a spark. And that can start a fire. If that happens, unplug the power cord if you can safely do so, and call the fire department. Never open the door or throw water on a microwave oven. You could make things worse.

video_title: How to Survive a Malfunctioning Microwave
text: It can be difficult to tell if your microwave is not working properly. That's why you'd better keep your distance, as Daniel S. should have done. In 2018, the young man was at his house in Morelia, Mexico, when his wife told him she was craving popcorn. He put a bag of popcorn in the microwave oven. Suddenly, a malfunction caused an electric shock, and the microwave oven exploded. He died almost immediately. No matter how hungry you are, keep your distance from a microwave oven.

video_title: How to Survive a Malfunctioning Microwave
text: Microwaves pass through paper, glass, and plastic containers. Then penetrate evenly into the food and liquids you're heating. That's why they cook food so quickly and evenly. But this efficiency can be really dangerous. Liquids can easily get heated past their boiling points before they have a chance to release the steam that boiling produces. This is called superheating, and it makes liquid dangerously unstable. At this point, even a tiny movement of the container could cause the liquid to erupt, burning your skin and even causing your body to go into shock. Avoid superheating by heating liquids for only short periods of time.

text: No matter how badly you need that reheated coffee, do not open the door before the timer goes off. It can cause a radiation leak and even serious astronomical confusion, as scientists at the Parkes Observatory in Australia discovered. For years, astronomers looked for the source of strange signals detected by the radio telescope. They called them "perytons." Some people began to speculate they were alien messages. But some years later, astronomers discovered they were caused by the microwave ovens in the break room when they were opened before the timer dinged. So, don’t be impatient.
